OCR/import issues (specifically scanned, image-only PDFs lacking a text layer) directly degrade both onboarding performance and the support/ingestion infrastructure.

**Impact on onboarding performance:**
- Scanned PDFs require OCR before reliable citation linking; without it, citation accuracy drops and customers fail the go-live quality checks (85% citation correctness threshold), delaying rollout [NL-015#NL-015-S04].
- OCR processing accounts for 25% of onboarding delay incidents [NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-031#NL-031-S04].
- Such files cause failed ingestion, incomplete text extraction, and missing/low-quality answers, forcing manual OCR pre-processing that adds weeks; e.g., Northstar Financial's pilot was delayed by three weeks [NL-010#NL-010-S06].
- BrightPath Healthcare experienced the longest onboarding (9.5 weeks) due to OCR/scanned PDF compliance issues, failing go-live validation because scanned PDFs return incomplete citations [NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-031#NL-031-S04].
- When go-live thresholds fail, the implementation lead pauses go-live and triggers a mandatory remediation path including corpus audits and content cleanup [NL-005#NL-005-S11].

**Impact on support/ingestion infrastructure performance:**
- Dumping thousands of scanned PDFs into the same queue as standard text-rich uploads causes OCR workers to block fast uploads, degrading overall ingestion performance; the March 14 incident (an import worker retry storm from a schema-migration config change) highlighted this risk [NL-021#NL-021-S06].
- To prevent queue clogging, a split-queue architecture (Fast Queue for text-based files vs. Batch/OCR Queue for scanned PDFs) with per-tenant concurrency limits (capped at 5 OCR threads) is required [NL-021#NL-021-S07][NL-021#NL-021-S06].
- OCR runs are resource-intensive (memory and worker load), so dedicated auto-scaling and per-plan document page caps (100/500/2,000 pages for Starter/Growth/Enterprise) are enforced to protect queue capacity [NL-021#NL-021-S06][NL-021#NL-021-S07].
